MGE Energy's ownership interest in ATC Holdco is held by MGEE Transco, a wholly-owned subsidiary of MGE Energy.

The ownership interest in ATC Holdco is held by MGEE Transco, a subsidiary of MGE Energy.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

intro.text: MGE Energy is a public utility holding company. Its principal subsidiary, Madison Gas and Electric, generates and distributes electricity to 170,000 customers in Dane County, Wis., and purchases and distributes natural gas to 180,000 customers in seven south-central and western Wisconsin counties. MGE's roots in the Madison area date back more than 150 years.

s.t: Electric operations accounted for approximately 72%, 74%, and 71% of MGE's total 2025, 2024, and 2023 regulated revenues, respectively.
Gas operations accounted for approximately 28%, 26%, and 29% of MGE's total 2025, 2024, and 2023 regulated revenues, respectively.
Based on results for the year ended December 31, 2025, no one customer constituted more than 10% of total operating revenues for MGE Energy and MGE.
Our ability to obtain adjustments to those rates depends upon timely regulatory action under applicable statutes and regulations.

The amount of credits earned depends on facility in-service dates and operating factors, including generation output, transmission constraints, pricing trends, adverse weather conditions, equipment reliability, and the applicable credit rates.
We could also be forced to replace lost generation capacity with additional power purchases from third parties, potentially leading to increased costs.
AI-driven energy management tools could also enable customers to optimize usage and further reduce purchases from us.

The Columbia plant operator has been, and the plant operators may be, forced to reduce generation at our jointly-held coal units, which would cause us to replace this generation through additional power purchases from third parties.
We also rely on our credit ratings to access the credit markets.
MGE relies on third parties to deliver its products and services to customers, and a cybersecurity incident at a supplier, subcontractor, or joint venture partner could materially impact MGE.
The amount and timing of any financings will be primarily driven by capital investments and cash requirements and will depend upon market conditions, regulatory approvals, and other factors.
The decrease in purchased power was due to an approximately 39% decrease in market purchases as a result of increased internal generation.
The principal sources and uses of cash are related to short-term and long-term borrowings and repayments and the payment of cash dividends.

MGE Energy's and MGE's access to the capital markets, including, in the case of MGE, the commercial paper market, and their respective financing costs in those markets, may depend on the credit ratings of the entity that is accessing the capital markets.
Final timing and retirement dates continue to be evaluated, and depend upon operational regulatory considerations, capacity needs, and availability.
The amount and timing of the cash impacts will depend on the period over which certain income tax benefits are provided to customers, which will be subject to review by the PSCW.
The actual payments upon vesting depends upon actual performance and may range from zero to 200 % of the granted number of performance units.
